content.title: Recommendations for clinical and diagnostic tools for patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome

recommendations.recommendation: Patients with suspected STEMI are immediately triaged for an emergency reperfusion strategy.

Base the diagnosis and initial short-term risk stratification of ACS on a combination of clinical history, symptoms, vital signs, other physical findings, ECG, and high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn).
Twelve-lead ECG recording and interpretation as soon as possible at the point of first medical contact, with a target of <10 min.

Continuous ECG monitoring and availability of defibrillator capacity as soon as possible in all patients with suspected STEMI, in suspected ACS with other ECG changes or ongoing chest pain, and once the diagnosis of MI is made.
Use additional ECG leads (V3R, V4R, and V7–V9) in cases of inferior STEMI or if total vessel occlusion is suspected and standard leads are inconclusive.
An additional 12-lead ECG is recommended in cases with recurrent symptoms or diagnostic uncertainty.
Measure cardiac troponins with high-sensitivity assays immediately after presentation and obtain results within 60 min of blood sampling.
Use an ESC algorithmic approach with serial hs-cTn measurements (0 h/1 h or 0 h/2 h) to rule in and rule out NSTEMI.
Additional testing after 3 h is recommended if the first two hs-cTn measurements of the 0 h/1 h algorithm are inconclusive and no alternative diagnoses explaining the condition have been made.
